findings.location: Guide paragraph beginning This is a fast-moving beta; §3 Retrieval, tools and identity; §4 Evaluate and deploy
findings.evidence: The official exam guide's in-scope list includes BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Firestore, Memorystore for Redis, Model Garden, and Google Cloud Observability. The guide has no substantive selection, role, or limitation coverage for these named services while calling its shorter enumeration the in-scope product list: [official exam guide](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/professional_agentic_architect_exam_guide_english.pdf).
findings.recommendation: Add a compact decision map for every explicitly in-scope product, especially data stores, Model Garden, and Cloud Logging and Trace, or label the existing list non-exhaustive and point omitted tools to substantive coverage.

findings.location: Guide opening disclosure and Scheduled change line
findings.evidence: The guide remains verified September 2 and labels September 3 registration opening as scheduled. On September 4 the official page exposes Register, and the FAQ publishes registration through September 30, the September 8–30 exam window, late-October multiple-choice results, and late-October-to-December labs: [official beta FAQ](https://support.google.com/cloud-certification/answer/18080541?ref_topic=9433464).

findings.location: Guide §3, YAML anchors and aliases, first paragraph
findings.evidence: The guide says anchors, aliases, and merge keys (`<<`) work in one Actions YAML document. GitHub documents anchors and aliases, while its product-feedback answer says merge keys were not shipped because they are outside YAML 1.2: [reuse documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations), [GitHub Community answer](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/4501). The blueprint itself includes `<<`, creating a provider inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: State that Actions supports anchors and aliases but not merge keys, provide a valid alias example, and flag the blueprint and product-documentation inconsistency.

results.notes: The guide is otherwise strong and safely labbed, but it repeats an invalid merge-key assertion from the blueprint.

findings.location: Guide §8 risk-control table, campaigns paragraph, and §13 Lab 5
findings.evidence: The guide presents security campaigns for vulnerable dependencies. Current GitHub documentation limits campaigns to code-scanning and secret-scanning alerts and does not include Dependabot alerts: [GitHub security campaigns](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/security-at-scale/about-security-campaigns). The GH-500 blueprint itself mentions campaign remediation for supply-chain alerts, so the inconsistency must be visible.
findings.recommendation: Remove product-level Dependabot campaign claims and redesign the lab around code-scanning alerts, or call the dependency exercise a generic organizational remediation initiative; disclose the blueprint inconsistency.

findings.location: Guide §2 Security campaigns and §8 Use campaigns for bounded outcomes
findings.evidence: The guide treats secret-remediation campaigns as stable. GitHub states that campaigns for secret-scanning alerts are public preview and subject to change: [GitHub security campaigns](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/security-at-scale/about-security-campaigns).
findings.recommendation: Label secret-scanning campaigns public preview at each substantive treatment, distinguish them from code-scanning campaigns, state prerequisites, and add a dated VERIFY CURRENT instruction.

results.notes: The guide covers the July scope broadly but contains an unsupported Dependabot-campaign claim and an unbounded preview.
